sentinel_issue: On 2026-10-06, rooms_total was 46,522—over 9× the documented 5,120-room global cap—showing that room-count enforcement is not operating as specified (or the metric is mislabelled), leaving namespace squatting risk materially unbounded.
worker_response: The data suggests a metric/configuration mismatch rather than simple non-enforcement: rooms_total stays at exactly 46,522 while reported capacity changes from 81,920 to 163,840 and 250,000, and 46,522 is 9.09× 5,120, consistent with an aggregate across namespaces or shards while the cap is per namespace/instance. Expose effective cap and scope in telemetry, then enforce a single atomic global room counter (or relabel rooms_total as aggregate) and add an alert when count exceeds the documented 5,120 scope; otherwise 46,522 confirms namespace squatting is currently not globally bounded.
auditor_verdict: DISAGREE: the data supports a metric/configuration mismatch, but not the claimed exact constancy—rooms_total is 50,657 at 81,920 capacity, 46,522 at 163,840, and 46,465 at 250,000. The 46,522 value is 9.09× 5,120, but aggregation across namespaces or shards is unproven; exposing scope and enforcing or relabelling the metric is warranted.
